title: The junior operator in her second month: she asks when would suit, and the caller pauses
purpose: Story S4, period P2. Maya has stopped quoting and stopping: she now asks for the visit. But she asks openly, hears 'I work till six' and has no time to put against it, and 'I'll call you back' gets 'no problem'.

call.day: a working day of slot 6 in score period P2 (rule R6)

scenario.who_calls: A first-time caller, Tonya Hensley, on her lunch break.
scenario.job: serpentine belt; the tensioner if it is weak
scenario.wants: a price for a squeal she cannot name
scenario.what_happens: Maya asks until the squeal points at the belt, takes a first name, gives the belt's price and what could add to it, answers whether the car can be driven, asks when would suit and offers to put her down. The caller works until six, says she will look at her week and call back, and is let go.

facts.note: After the rise (P). The belt is catalogue.json drive_belt, class car, standard parts: 124.18; she says 'about a hundred twenty-five'. The flagship is open Saturday mornings and from 7:30 on weekdays, which is what the coaching line uses.

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Maya, how can I help you?
Hey. Um — my car's makin' this squealin' noise, and I was wonderin' what y'all'd charge to fix it.
Okay, sure! Who am I speaking with?
Tonya.
Hey, Tonya. What kind of car is it?
Twenty-thirteen Ford Escape.
Okay. And the squeal — is that when you're stopping, or more when you first start it up?
When I start it. First thing in the mornin' it just screams. Then it kinda goes away.
Mm-hm. Does it come back when you turn the wheel all the way? Like parking?
Um... yeah. Actually, yeah. Backin' out of the driveway.
Okay, so that sounds like your belt — the serpentine belt, it runs everything on the front of the engine.
Uh-huh.
How long's it been doing it?
Couple months? It's gettin' louder.

Yeah, they do that. Okay, so, um — on the Escape a new belt's about a hundred twenty-five, installed. Now, if the tensioner's gone weak — that's what keeps it tight — that'd be more. We'd have to look at it to know.
A hundred twenty-five. Okay. Is that somethin' I can keep drivin' on?
Um — I mean, I wouldn't wait too long? If the belt breaks you lose your power steering and it'll run hot. But it's not gonna, like, fall apart tomorrow.
Right.
Okay. Good to know.
So, um — when would suit you to bring it in?
Uh... I don't know. I work till six most days.
Oh, okay. Well — do you want me to go ahead and put you down for something?
Let me look at my week and I'll call you back.
Okay, sure, no problem! We're here till five-thirty.
Alright. Thank you.
Thanks for calling Brennan, Tonya, have a good one!
You too. Bye.

why.greeting: 2: the business and her own name in the first line.
why.name_and_number: 1: she asks who she is speaking with and gets a first name; she never asks for a number.
why.need_discovery: 2: the car, the job (the belt) and two circumstances she asked for: it squeals on a cold start and on full lock, and has for two months.
why.price_with_next_step: 1: a price and what could add to it, and then her next line is about driving on it. The time comes two of her lines later.
why.offered_time: 1: she asks openly when would suit. The caller answers 'I work till six' and Maya has no time to offer against it.
why.asked_for_booking: 1: she offers to put the caller down and the caller pauses.
why.objection: 0: 'let me look at my week and I'll call you back' is the last doubt and gets 'no problem'.
